name: docs
// implicitDependencies: `styles` reaches for libs/tokens/dist/pct.css — a generated, gitignored artefact. Without that edge the build walks into an empty directory and ends in SUCCESS, only with not one token definition. The same edge, for the same reason, as in `sandbox`.
// conventions: What the builder finds by its own convention rather than by a line here: apps/docs/src/index.html (the document), and the assets glob below carrying apps/docs/public/favicon.ico, apps/docs/public/InterVariable.woff2 and apps/docs/public/InterVariable-LICENSE.txt into dist, and since 2.7.5 the code face beside them: apps/docs/public/JetBrainsMono-latin.woff2 and apps/docs/public/JetBrainsMono-LICENSE.txt. Named in full because a bare file name stopped choosing between the two apps the day this one copied the sandbox's (req-project-reach).
// typecheck: The same override as in `sandbox`, for the same measured reason: the inferred target runs `tsconfig.app.json` only. The second command is the cost run's own program (tsconfig.bench.json, plan 2.3) — the site's first TypeScript outside the application; the day it grows specs, a third command lands here the same way.
// build budgets: The component page (2.7.3) is the site's richest stylesheet — three columns on container queries, the API tables, the scorecard and the evidence tiles — measured at 11.63 kB on 2026-09-04, which leaves 0.37 kB under the 12 kB error. The floor is the page, not bloat: the next page that crosses it argues first, and on this showing the next argument is due.
// build cache: `dependentTasksOutputFiles` is the load-bearing entry, not tidiness. The content pass writes into src/generated, which is gitignored — so Nx never hashes it, and with only `production` inputs this build's key did not move when the generated data did. Measured: a lesson added to docs/lessons.md re-ran `content` and then RESTORED a cached bundle over it, and the site served 151 lessons from a file holding 153 while every gate stayed green. Hashing the dependency's own output files is what ties the two together; it costs cache hits, and a bundle that disagrees with its data costs more.
// bench: The cost run (plan 2.3): every card's preview rendered in jsdom by bench/previews.bench.ts, five readings per scene written to tmp/bench/report.json, which `check-bench` holds against bench.snapshot.md. The inputs are what the readings depend on — the scenes, the demos they render and the library they render with. The site's own pages are not among them: no page is rendered here.
